records.summary: Locate the Steam install of Shadow of War without hardcoded paths.
Produce a read-only PE inventory of the exe and bundled DLLs.
Static probe of section contents to judge suitability for Ghidra analysis.
Run the prototype unit, integration and network test suites (Phase 1 tests 1-12).
End-to-end run of the real executables: one mordor-host and two mordor-client processes on 127.0.0.1 with 40 ms latency, 20 ms jitter and 10% loss on every sender.
Explain an E2E run where the host received 0 packets and both clients failed with connect_timeout.
Direct LAN test between two physical PCs.
Independent code review of the networking prototype, as required by the project's collaboration rules.
Verify and address ChatGPT review #1 findings FB-1-01 (host backlog timestep), FB-1-02 (state-aware liveness) and FB-1-07 (reconnect edge cases) with regression tests.
Real-time soak of host + 2 clients under three impairment profiles with a mid-run client stall (review FB-1-03 P1).
Verify and address ChatGPT review #2 (FB-2-01 manifest validation, FB-2-02 timeout-notice robustness, FB-2-03 budgets) and re-run the soak under gate version 2.
Address ChatGPT's review #2 follow-up (manifest well-formedness and scenario match; mean vs peak bandwidth) as soak gate version 3 and re-run the soak.
GameNetworkingSockets spike (D-012): build it via vcpkg and measure reliability and default security on loopback.

ChatGPT review #3: implement the Transport interface with the existing UDP backend without changing any test (FB-3-02), verify GNS authentication facts against the real library (answer 1), and harden the GNS spike tests (FB-3-01/03/04/05).
ChatGPT review #4: finalize the Transport contract (identity, lifecycle, delivery classes, errors) before the GNS adapter, keep UDP behaviour, and add backend-independent contract tests.
Implement the GameNetworkingSockets adapter behind Transport contract v2 and validate it with the UNCHANGED contract, host/client and soak suites (ChatGPT recommendation after review #4).
Implement ChatGPT review #5 FB-5-01..04 and the owner-approved FB-5-05 DTLS 1.2 + RFC 7250 proof test.

Implement ChatGPT review #6 FB-6-01..05: fail-closed invitation binding, DTLS over a real Transport::Unreliable link on both backends, KI-27 root cause, wording, separate-process asymmetric scenarios; plus the bounded connect-deadline policy.
Implement ChatGPT review #7 FB-7-01..05 and answer 3 (secure transport decorator); prepare the KI-27 upstream report for the owner.
Refine the KI-27 upstream draft: check upstream master, search duplicates, discriminate first Init vs re-Init, verify a standalone Windows build, audit for private information.
Implement ChatGPT review #8 FB-8-01..05: cookie-aware pending replacement, secure reliable channel, key/invitation provisioning with secure executables and E2E/soak, idle timeout, KI-27 wording.
Implement ChatGPT review #9 FB-9-01..05 including application-level reliable events (protocol v2) and soak gate v5 (realized impairment).

Implement ChatGPT review #10 (FB-10-01..05 and answer 5) on feature/ki35-ki37-investigation: EventAck bounded by sent ids, events marked sent only on Sent, stateless DTLS cookie gate, explicit leave handshake (protocol v3), KI-35 instrumentation, soak gate v6; investigate KI-35 and KI-37 from traces before any tuning.

Implement ChatGPT review #11 (FB-11-01..05) on feature/review11-gns-readiness: measure, then gate the secure client's DTLS start on the inner GNS Connected; departure edge cases; cookie and coalescing checks; full v6 battery at HEAD with seeded harsh repeats.

Implement ChatGPT review #12 (FB-12-01..05) on feature/review12-retry-experiment: a predeclared one-variable experiment on the session reconnect retry, KI-40 lifecycle diagnosis, the GNS return-routability question, more departure tests, then the full v6 battery with seeded repeats.

Implement ChatGPT reviews #13/#14 (FB-13-01..03, FB-14-01..03) on feature/review13-14-followup and validate the final head of the #12-#15 stack: harness hardening, KI-41 contract, secure E2E barrier, a predeclared UDP-only retry experiment, GNS phase distributions, full v6 battery with seeded repeats.

Implement ChatGPT review #15 (FB-15-01..05) on feature/review15-followup: verify GNS return routability from source, investigate KI-42 and KI-40, run the predeclared GNS-only DTLS cookie A/B with negative security tests, and validate the head with the full v6 battery.

Implement ChatGPT review #16 (FB-16-01..03) on feature/review16-followup: bound the stack-dump diagnostic inside Wait-Bounded and hang-watch, make compare_arms.py refuse a verdict on empty or non-finite cohorts, and shut GNS down on every exit path of mordor-host and mordor-client.

Implement ChatGPT review #17 (FB-17-01/02) on feature/review17-evidence: document the dump limit, make test evidence immutable per run, recover the evidence that date-named files lost, and enforce the rule.

Implement ChatGPT review #18 on feature/review18-repeat: keep every test.ps1 -Repeat invocation with its exit code (FB-18-01), show each suite's run status in the report (FB-18-02), and qualify the wait budget (FB-18-03) and the meaning of a creation snapshot (FB-18-04).

Implement ChatGPT review #19 on feature/review19-freshness: a bounded recent-runs history with every invocation's exit code in the report (FB-19-01), and result freshness without timestamps plus failing missing suites (FB-19-02).

Implement ChatGPT review #20 on feature/review20-validation: persist the failure reason of a run stopped by an error (FB-20-01), validate result files beyond their presence (FB-20-02), and show commit and clean/dirty on recent-run lines (FB-20-03).

Implement ChatGPT review #21 on feature/review21-identity: FAILED cases fail the run whatever ctest's exit code (FB-21-01), suite identity in the runner's JSON (FB-21-02), redaction of paths with spaces and non-ASCII letters (FB-21-03).

Implement ChatGPT review #22 on feature/review22-escaping: JSON escaping of every string field in the C++ test runner (FB-22-01), and provenance with digests for restored and missing per-invocation evidence (FB-22-02); record the closure of PRs #1-#21 and the consolidation in PR #22.

Run the integration gate (docs/integration-gate.md, review #23 FB-23-02) on an exact candidate head that contains the whole stack (PR #22) and its follow-ups (#23 and this branch), and record what a merge into main would and would not establish.

Second run of the integration gate (docs/integration-gate.md) after Codex passes 6 and 7 on candidate 2217085 found 3 P2 defects, plus 1 more found by the combined pass on the fixed head; record what it establishes before the two consecutive clean Codex passes (FB-24-01).

Third run of the integration gate items 3-5, on 3607613: the candidate after the fixes found by the combined Codex passes on 9904293..40b02c5 (peer sharing on token migration, a reused client, protocol v4 per-player event and leave messages, the CMake manifest cache, E2E log quoting and bounded E2E waits).
Fourth run of the integration gate, on the candidate head 3c618d9, after item 2 reached two consecutive clean Codex passes on that unchanged head (FB-24-01).
The GitHub org Shadow-of-War-Modding-Community has exactly three public repos (ImHex-Patterns, MeshParser, Documentation); none declares a license and Documentation contains only a one-line README.
Community research identifies arch06 archives by the 4-byte magic 'LTAR' followed by a u32 version, but the public ImHex pattern maps only a short header and no file table, compression or index.

The community magic file lists ten Shadow of War asset formats by magic: LTAR (arch06), BNDL, EMBB, LTFX (fxp), GADB (gamedb), LTMI (mat), MMSH (mesh), SCRI (scripts), SKEL and SKDB (strdb), each followed by a u32 version.

The game database format (magic GADB) is only partly understood publicly: header, a string table and hashed string pointers are mapped, while record blocks remain 'unknown' and use hardcoded file offsets.
Community patterns show SKEL files are sectioned (bone, model, animation, indices, cloth, footer) with bones identified by 32-bit name hashes; 364 bone-name hashes are published.
MeshParser (MeshUnpacker) is a Windows C++ tool that converts SoW .mesh (magic MMSH) to/from FBX via Assimp, supporting static meshes only, and the repo ships prebuilt Assimp DLL/LIB binaries.
Shadow of War runs on Monolith's Firebird engine, described as a LithTech-derived successor to the engine used in Shadow of Mordor.

ReaperAnon's Middle-Earth-Mod-Loader is a bink2w64.dll proxy (original renamed bink2w64_.dll) that loads plugin DLLs from a plugins folder, uses MinHook and a byte-pattern scan of ShadowOfWar.exe, and exposes a small menu/log plugin API.

survivalizeed's ShadowOfWarPacketLoader replaces game resources at load time by hooking the engine's main file-read routine and swapping chunk bytes matched by stored signatures; it is installed as a plugin of the mod loader.

PC saves are single files named <uid>_ShadowOfWar.sav under %LOCALAPPDATA%\WB Games\Shadow of War, starting with magic 'SOM3' and AES-CBC encrypted with a key built from a fixed template, header bytes and the 32-bit id in the filename.

Third-party tools indicate the Nemesis system is named 'Faction' internally, with runtime script variables such as Faction.Debug.* and FactionMember.Debug.Resurrection and one-byte debug-channel flags in the exe's data section.

The game's online services use WB's backend at kraken-api.wbagora.com with a custom zlib-compressed binary value protocol and endpoints /auth, /access, /ssc/invoke and /broadcast_channels; a community rebuild of this server exists.

Shadow of War's official online features (Online Conquest, Online Vendettas, social/fight-pit modes) are asynchronous; the predecessor Shadow of Mordor's online features were shut down in January 2021 while Shadow of War's were stated to remain unaffected, and no official 2025-2026 shutdown notice was found.

There is no primary-source evidence that Denuvo was removed from the Steam version; the Steam store page still declares 'Denuvo Antitamper' on 2026-10-23, so the 'removed later' claim is contradicted by available sources.

The Shadow of War EULA prohibits modifying the game client (1c), reverse engineering or deriving source code (1d), cheats/hacks or unauthorized third-party programs (1e), and software that interacts with the client or emulates WB's protocols (1b), and allows connecting to WB game servers only with an unmodified authorized client (1g-1h); it has no mod-specific allowance.
Warner Bros holds US patent 10,926,179 B2 on Nemesis characters, forts, social vendettas and followers, granted 2021-02-23 and listed by Google Patents as active until 2036-08-11.

Per PCGamingWiki, the Steam build requires Denuvo whose regular servers include srv01-srv03 and revalidate.wbgames.com, while the Microsoft Store build appears to lack Denuvo; GOG sells a DRM-free version.
Monolith Productions was closed by Warner Bros on 2025-02-25, so further patches to Shadow of War are unlikely and build 3095001 is a stable target.

SystematicSkid's sow-freecam hooks the camera transform update via a call-site signature with MinHook and reaches the camera through a GameClient object whose camera owner pointer sits at a fixed offset.

A third-party research repo (cranebeaker/coop-anything) documents Shadow of War co-op research claiming the exact target build (1.0.8874.0, build 3095001, same SHA-256), including a console-variable registry, a stubbed debug_print and a central Nemesis event handler, and lists JustAddMP/ShadowOfWar as a README-only 'planned' co-op placeholder.

GitHub search for 'shadow of war' returns several recently created 'Cheats'/'Trainer' repos by unknown accounts that have no relation to the modding community and must be treated as likely malware lures.
coop-anything (MIT) defines a 9-phase workflow for adding co-op to single-player games: triage, research, workspace, understand (RE), choose, build, QA, ship, give back.

The playbook recommends host-authoritative state sync with network-driven puppets for remote players as the default for closed native single-player games, and rejects lockstep unless the engine is already deterministic.
The repo's NPC/AI model is exactly one owner machine per actor, chosen by the host, with an epoch counter that rejects stale or echoed updates and a handshake-based ownership handoff.
For story state the repo proposes 'effect capture': only the host runs story scripts, records each primitive world change, and clients apply that ordered effect list instead of re-running scripts.
The playbook treats the host's save as canonical, makes client saving a no-op or separate slot, and uses a full snapshot on join (then deltas) as late-join, reconnect and test oracle.
The repo's default stack is Steam relay via ISteamNetworkingMessages (often on AppID 480 Spacewar) for connectivity, with ENet or GameNetworkingSockets as the C++ transport for custom netcode.
Desync detection in the repo uses an always-on flight recorder plus 256-bucket additive state digests to locate the first divergent key, then ddmin shrinking into a regression fixture.

The repo prescribes seeded network impairment testing with six profiles (lan to hell) shared between a UDP relay and an in-process C++ simulator, asserting convergence, no double apply and bounded recovery.
The repo's QA policy forbids human playtests as the test plan and requires in-game bots, two or more real clients, mutation twins and hollow-pass guards for any 'works' claim.

The repo's tool catalogue covers Ghidra headless, IDA/Ghidra MCPs, REA, x64dbg, Cheat Engine, ReClass.NET, Frida, Process Monitor, MinHook, Detours, PolyHook 2 and SafetyHook, preferring static analysis first.

The repo contains a Shadow of War write-up stating the game runs on Firebird (internal 'Kraken'), a LithTech derivative whose source paths keep a client/server split, NetMesh hosting port and host-vote state machine, runtime use unverified.

The repo reports that Shadow of War's Nemesis ('Faction') logic runs on one game thread, dispatches every event through HandleFactionEventAction (RVA 40C304), and draws outcomes from one global 64-bit LCG.

The repo documents that an isolated Shadow of War test copy still leaked: steam.exe wrote test saves into the real Steam userdata via ISteamRemoteStorage even with Steam Cloud off, and NVIDIA App rewrote the real render.cfg.

The repo's ground rules forbid anti-cheat bypass and touching the owner's install or saves, but its agent workflow also expects git pull, gh issue/PR use, draft PRs under the owner's GitHub account, and an auto-configured MCP server; Project Mordor must not grant these.

The repo reports that the SoW save editor's fixed function RVAs do not fit Steam build 3095001 while byte-pattern signatures do, and that hooking tiny leaf stubs must preserve volatile registers or the game crashes.
The installed game is Steam app 356190, buildid 3095001, ShadowOfWar.exe FileVersion 1.0.8874.0 with SHA-256 ED0D95CA...0BDAEF.
No proxy-DLL mod loader is installed in the game x64 directory.
The executable's entry point is in a section named .bind with entropy 7.947, a layout consistent with the Steam DRM (SteamStub) wrapper.
The section table is atypical for an MSVC build (names such as .arch, .xtext, '.bss a', .srdata; flags inconsistent with names) and the static import table holds only 199 functions from 21 DLLs.
The executable exports Wwise (AK::SoundEngine) and Scaleform symbols, so it statically links the Audiokinetic Wwise audio and Autodesk Scaleform UI middleware.
The static import table imports winhttp.dll and wininet.dll (HTTP) and steam_api64.dll but no ws2_32.dll. Any socket networking is not visible in static imports.
game/projectconsole.cfg sets 'GameClientShell.LoadUnprefetchedResources 0'. GameClientShell is LithTech-family naming.
A per-user directory '%LOCALAPPDATA%/WB Games/Shadow of War' exists. Its contents were deliberately not inspected in Phase 1.

The owner's copy is the GOG release: GOG store metadata (goggame-1324471032.info/.hashdb/.script) and GOG's uninstaller are present, and no crack or Steam-emulator file is. Its executable is a different build from the Steam one (FileVersion 1.0.2445.0, 44,473,856 bytes, versus 1.0.8874.0 at about 114 MB). It still ships Valve's validly signed steam_api64.dll.

The GOG executable shows none of the Steam build's wrapper indicators: its entry point is in .text and its sections are a conventional MSVC layout, with no .bind section, whereas the Steam build enters in .bind (entropy 7.947, F-ENV-003).
The GOG release starts and is playable with no Steam client and no GOG Galaxy client running.

In GameNetworkingSockets v1.6.1 a direct-UDP listen socket accepts a ConnectRequest only if it echoes a stateless challenge, a SipHash of (time slot, sender IP, sender port) under a per-socket secret, at most about 4 s old. A GNS connection therefore proves return routability for its address before it is created.

In GameNetworkingSockets v1.6.1, packets arriving on a shared direct-UDP listen socket are dispatched by source address: an accepted connection is registered under its remote address (CSharedSocket::AddRemoteHost) and receives only packets from that address; any other source goes to the listen socket's unknown-address handler (challenge / connect / close messages). Together with F-GNS-001, data on an established GNS connection comes only from the address that answered the stateless challenge.
SoWLoader is a hand-written steam_api64.dll proxy that forwards all 796 Steam exports to a renamed steam_api64_org.dll and starts a worker thread from DllMain.
The repo reports that ShadowOfWar.exe statically imports steam_api64.dll (shipped in x64\) and delay-loads d3d11.dll and amd_ags_x64.dll, making steam_api64.dll the chosen proxy injection point.

SoWLoader loads external mod DLLs from <install>\mods\ in filename order and calls an optional exported SoWMod_Init(int page) on its worker thread, with optional SoWMod_Name/SoWMod_Scope exports and a versioned HagUI_GetAPI ABI.

The repo reports the Steam ShadowOfWar.exe is wrapped by SteamStub v3.1 (removed with Steamless; .text not encrypted) plus Denuvo Anti-Tamper woven into code, with a near-empty .text and real code in .xtext/.arch sections, image base 0x140000000.

All game addresses in the repo are hardcoded file RVAs (off image base 0x140000000) in shared/GameOffsets.h converted at runtime via FromRVA; there is no pattern/signature scanning and no game version, buildid or exe-hash check anywhere in the repo.

SoWLoader installs MinHook trampoline hooks (call-original, non-destructive) on five hardcoded game functions: CUIFrontEndRootLayer ctor, OnWorldLoad, save-to-front-end clear, front-end item refresh, and the per-frame cursor recenter, the last of which drains a 128-slot game-thread task queue.

Repo claims game-function RVAs for the main thread/window (0x140c24db0), post-window init (0x1411798ac), world load (0x141c3d7fc), save-to-front-end clear (0x141bb8e30) and cursor recenter (0x1411ac828), several described as live-verified by the author.
The repo identifies the engine as Monolith LithTech lineage ('Kraken' ClientShell) with a data-driven Scaleform (GFx) front-end UI and a global StringDatabase localization function.

The repo's RE workflow is fully manual: Ghidra 12.1.2 headless analysis of a Steamless-unpacked exe with ~25 helper Java scripts (RTTI, VtableDump, FindXrefs, Trace, DumpUI, etc.); no existing community SoW framework is used.

The InventoryEditor mod obtains the current player as *(*(engine singleton 0x1426ffa98)+0x888) and reads the player world position as three floats at player+0x2180/0x2184/0x2188, although GameOffsets.h marks that engine singleton as UNVERIFIED.

Repo claims items can be spawned as world pickups via a game-systems singleton (0x1426ffaa8, +0x6d28 world drop manager) and functions LootRecordInit/FromItem/Destroy and WorldDropSpawn(pose, lootRecord, id, worldCtx, flag), mirroring Combat.Action.InventoryItemDropLoot.

The overlay subclasses the game window procedure (SetWindowLongPtrW GWLP_WNDPROC) and swallows WM_INPUT raw input while the hub is open, implying the game uses Win32 Raw Input for mouselook; the repo also claims a global cursor-control gate at 0x1427030c8.

The repo maps no camera, character-controller, combat, AI, Nemesis/orc, mission or save-game structures; the only 'camera' handling is blocking raw input, and pause/sim time-scale is explicitly unsolved.

Repo claims a time-scale request system: the pause menu OnActivate (0x141961068) pushes a SimulationTimeScale request via 0x14046bdec, with a time-scale manager at 0x1426ffb08+0x70, and that the game does not pause on focus loss.

The only networking in the repo is HagIPC, a dev-only loopback TCP (127.0.0.1, default port 19000) text server injected via CreateRemoteThread(LoadLibraryW) that offers memory read/write, arbitrary function call, code-blob exec, MinHook probe hooks, watch and value scan; there is no game-to-game networking or Steam networking use.

The repo states game data is packed in Oodle-compressed .arch06 archives (oo2core_5_win64.dll) and that the item database game.gamedb (magic 'GADB', ~55 MB) can be extracted from Patch_02.arch06 with QuickBMS's shadow_of_mordor.bms script.
The repository has no LICENSE/COPYING file and no license statement in README or manifests, so by default all rights are reserved and its code cannot be copied into Project Mordor without permission.

The repo is a very recent, AI-assisted, fast-moving workspace (HEAD dated 2026-07-04, most commits are automatic 'Codex/Claude Stop hook' commits) and contains .claude/.codex hook configs that auto-commit and push.
